skill.name: multi-agent-brainstorming
skill.description: Runs a structured, sequential multi-agent design review with defined reviewer roles, decision logging, and exit criteria.
skill.summary: Use scoped reviewer agents to stress-test designs before implementation.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All four static findings are false positives. The two backtick findings are Markdown references to a brainstorming skill, and the blocker findings are design-review process guidance. No prompt injection or malicious intent was found in SKILL.md.

static_findings.snippet: No design is considered valid without a completed log.
> “If this design fails, did we do everything reasonable to catch it early?”

finding_verdicts.reason: The backticks mark the word brainstorming as inline Markdown code in prose. No shell command, interpolation, or execution instruction appears at this line.
This is a numbered process step that references the standard brainstorming skill using Markdown formatting. It does not invoke a shell or pass user input to a command.
This line requires a completed decision log before accepting a design. It does not request host, network, account, or environment inspection.
The quoted question is a design-review reflection prompt. It contains no reconnaissance, privilege request, or instruction to inspect the system.

content.value_statement: Single-agent ideation can miss risks, constraints, and user impact. This skill coordinates scoped reviewer roles to challenge designs before implementation.
actual_capabilities: Defines a primary designer role and separate reviewer roles.
Guides sequential review by skeptic, constraint guardian, and user advocate roles.
Requires a decision log with objections, alternatives, and rationale.
Uses an arbiter role to accept, reject, or require revisions.
Defines exit criteria before implementation can begin.
limitations: It is a process guide, not an automated multi-agent runtime.
It depends on the model following the stated role boundaries.
It does not validate technical claims with external tools.
It can slow simple decisions that need fast execution.

use_cases.title: Architecture Review
use_cases.description: Stress-test a proposed technical design before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Product Concept Review
use_cases.description: Evaluate assumptions, user impact, and scope risks in a new product idea.

use_cases.title: Operational Risk Review
use_cases.description: Check reliability, security, cost, and maintainability concerns before committing to a plan.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Simple Idea
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review for a small design decision.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use multi-agent brainstorming to review this idea: [idea]. Keep the decision log concise.

prompt_templates.title: Assess a Technical Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review for an implementation plan.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the structured review process on this plan: [plan]. Include assumptions, objections, revisions, and final disposition.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Design Alternatives
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review when several options are possible.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the reviewer roles to compare these alternatives: [options]. Record accepted objections and rejected objections with rationale.

prompt_templates.title: Gate a High-Risk Decision
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before approval of a risky project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the full process to this high-risk decision: [decision]. Do not approve until every exit criterion is satisfied.

output_examples.output: The review identifies unclear defaults, missing error states, and one accepted revision. The final disposition is REVISE with a short rationale.

output_examples.input: Evaluate a database migration plan before implementation.
output_examples.output: The process records assumptions, operational risks, reviewer objections, and mitigation decisions. The arbiter approves only after rollback planning is complete.

output_examples.input: Compare two approaches for a billing workflow.
output_examples.output: The skill separates design, critique, user impact, and arbitration. It produces a decision log and recommends one approach with noted tradeoffs.

best_practices: Start with clear requirements and constraints before invoking reviewer roles.
Keep each reviewer scoped to its assigned mandate.
Record every accepted or rejected objection in the decision log.
anti_patterns: Do not let reviewers add unrelated features during critique.
Do not approve a design before unresolved objections are addressed.
Do not use the process for trivial choices with low risk.

faq.question: Does this skill run agents automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides a structured process for role-based review within the current AI workflow.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it when a design needs risk reduction, formal review, or stronger confidence before implementation.

faq.question: Can it help with non-code ideas?
faq.answer: Yes. The roles can review product, process, documentation, and operational ideas.

faq.question: What is the decision log?
faq.answer: It is a record of decisions, alternatives, objections, resolutions, and rationale.

faq.question: What final outcomes can it produce?
faq.answer: It can produce APPROVED, REVISE, or REJECT with a brief rationale.

faq.question: Does it replace expert review?
faq.answer: No. It improves preparation and critique, but expert validation is still needed for high-risk decisions.
